newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss deny they laundered Nazi gold for Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Swiss deny they laundered Nazi gold for Portugal.

text.p: Switzerland's central bank denied on Friday that it had laundered looted Nazi gold for Portugal during World War Two and said it was "malevolent" of the World Jewish Congress (WJC) to suggest that it had.

The WJC released a U.S. intelligence document from 1944 on Thursday that said Portugal used the Swiss National Bank (SNB) to swap 20 tonnes of Nazi gold for Swiss bullion held in the U.S. Federal Reserve Bank and the Bank of Canada.

The swap aimed to eliminate evidence that Portugal was receiving gold looted by the Nazis, the document said. The Allies had warned Portugal and other neutral nations they would face reprisals if they bought looted German gold.
WJC Vice President Kalman Sultanik described the transaction as "a classic money-laundering operation".

"The bad guys win all around. The Nazis have sold their gold. The Portuguese have swapped their looted gold for clean gold and the Swiss National Bank earns commissions on each transaction," he said. "All it took was a few strokes of the pen."
But SNB spokesman Werner Abegg took issue with this interpretation, contending the Allies knew of and approved the transactions.

"Switzerland needed authorisation from the Allies to use gold that was frozen in its accounts in New York and Canada. The motivation was for Switzerland to get back some of that gold that was blocked and it could not use," he said.

"The whole story that...Switzerland helped in a laundering operation for German gold bought by Portugal is entirely wrong," he said, adding the SNB did not earn commissions on gold transactions between central banks.
"This whole statement really shows quite a bit of malevolence on the part of the WJC," he added.

The SNB has acknowledged it bought gold from Nazi Germany that it should have suspected was stolen from the countries and peoples conquered by Hitler's troops. It also held gold on behalf of other central banks that was used at times to finance trade.
But Abegg said the Allies backed Switzerland's open policy toward gold trade as long as looted gold was not changing hands.

"The reproach against Switzerland is always that it acted secretly without heeding Allied statements or warnings. That is what is always being implied, and that it acted for profit. That is not the case here," he insisted.
The 20 tonnes of gold was worth $24 million in the 1940s and would be valued at about $220 million today.
